book.title: Frankenstein · Chapter 8 — The Trial of Justine
book.author: Mary Shelley, Frankenstein (1831), Chapter 8

cast.name: Victor
cast.canonical: a lean, slightly hunched young man with untidy dark hair, round glasses, dark shadowed feverish eyes, wearing a stained lab apron
cast.anchor: round glasses, a stained lab apron and dark shadowed eyes

cast.name: Elizabeth
cast.role: cousin & beloved — gentle, devoted, the family's moral heart
cast.canonical: a gentle graceful young woman with bright fair golden hair in a long braid under a white bonnet, an oval locket at her throat and a shoulder shawl
cast.anchor: bright fair golden hair, a white bonnet, an oval locket and a shawl

cast.name: Justine
cast.role: servant girl — sweet, devoted, tragically wronged
cast.canonical: a slight sweet-faced young servant girl in a white servant's cap and a plain apron-dress, hands gently clasped, anxious gentle face
cast.anchor: a white servant's cap and clasped hands

cast.name: Alphonse
cast.role: father — wise, loving patriarch and magistrate
cast.canonical: a tall stooped elderly gentleman, balding grey hair, a long white beard, leaning on a walking cane, in a long coat
cast.anchor: a long white beard and a walking cane (elderly, stooped)

panels.scene: a solemn crowded 18th-century courtroom, the bespectacled dark-haired young man seated among his family in the gallery, rigid with hidden torment, shadowed eyes fixed on the empty dock
panels.composition: wide establishing courtroom, focus on the anguished young man

teen.narration: THE FAMILY IS SUMMONED TO COURT. VICTOR ALONE KNOWS THE TRUTH.

bubbles.text: During the whole of this wretched mockery of justice I suffered living torture.
It was to be decided whether the result of my curiosity and lawless devices would cause the death of two of my fellow beings
My own agitation and anguish was extreme during the whole trial

panels.scene: a calm young servant woman in a plain white servant's cap and mourning dress standing in the prisoner's dock, composed and quietly beautiful, thousands of unseen eyes upon her
panels.composition: close on Justine in the dock, dignified

teen.narration: JUSTINE STANDS ACCUSED OF LITTLE WILLIAM'S MURDER.

bubbles.text: The appearance of Justine was calm. She was dressed in mourning
she appeared confident in innocence and did not tremble
her countenance, always engaging, was rendered, by the solemnity of her feelings, exquisitely beautiful

panels.scene: a close view of the servant woman in the white cap in the dock, a single tear dimming her eye as she catches sight of the family, a look of sorrowful affection
panels.composition: close, a silent tear of recognition

teen.narration: SHE FINDS THEIR FACES IN THE CROWD.

bubbles.text: A tear seemed to dim her eye when she saw us, but she quickly recovered herself
a look of sorrowful affection seemed to attest her utter guiltlessness

panels.scene: a coarse market-woman on the witness stand pointing an accusing finger, the judges leaning in gravely, gaslight and dark wood, the servant woman small in the dock beyond

teen.narration: STRANGE FACTS PILE UP AGAINST HER.

bubbles.text: Several strange facts combined against her, which might have staggered anyone who had not such proof of her innocence as I had.
She had been out the whole of the night on which the murder had been committed

panels.scene: a golden-haired young woman with a long braid under a white bonnet and an oval locket, standing faltering as a small painted miniature is held up as evidence, the court stirring in horror

teen.narration: THE LOCKET FROM WILLIAM'S NECK IS PRODUCED — FOUND ON JUSTINE.

bubbles.text: a murmur of horror and indignation filled the court
Justine was called on for her defence.
an hour before the child had been missed, she had placed round his neck

panels.scene: the servant woman in the white cap in the dock, gathering her courage, speaking in a steady but trembling voice, hand pressed to her heart, sorrow and dignity

teen.narration: JUSTINE SPEAKS IN HER OWN DEFENCE.

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: God knows... how entirely I am innocent.

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: I rest my innocence on a plain and simple explanation of the facts which have been adduced against me

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: But I do not pretend that my protestations should acquit me

panels.scene: a moonlit night vignette of a lonely barn outside the shut gates of Geneva, a small cloaked figure of the servant woman sheltering, searching for a lost child, cold and afraid
panels.composition: wide, the innocent explanation of her lost night

teen.narration: SHE HAD SPENT THAT NIGHT LOST, SEARCHING FOR WILLIAM.

bubbles.text: she was forced to remain several hours of the night in a barn belonging to a cottage

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: Concerning the picture she could give no account.

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: I believe that I have no enemy on earth, and none surely would have been so wicked as to destroy me wantonly
She was alarmed by this account and passed several hours in looking for him

panels.scene: the golden-haired young woman with the braided bonnet and oval locket rising impassioned to address the court, one hand raised, earnest and brave, faces turned toward her

teen.narration: ELIZABETH RISES TO SPEAK FOR HER FRIEND.

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: when I see a fellow creature about to perish through the cowardice of her pretended friends, I wish to be allowed to speak

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: I believe and rely on her perfect innocence

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: During all that period she appeared to me the most amiable and benevolent of human creatures

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: She had no temptation for such an action

panels.scene: a hostile courtroom crowd, faces twisted with indignation and contempt, fists and murmurs turned against the small servant woman weeping in the dock

teen.narration: BUT THE CROWD ONLY HARDENS AGAINST HER.

bubbles.text: the public indignation was turned with renewed violence, charging her with the blackest ingratitude
She herself wept as Elizabeth spoke, but she did not answer
but it was excited by her generous interference

panels.scene: the bespectacled dark-haired young man stumbling out through the heavy courtroom doors into a stone corridor, clutching his chest in agony, shadowed eyes wild with guilt

teen.narration: VICTOR CANNOT BEAR IT — HE FLEES.

bubbles.text: I rushed out of the court in agony.
the fangs of remorse tore my bosom and would not forgo their hold
The tortures of the accused did not equal mine; she was sustained by innocence
I passed a night of unmingled wretchedness

panels.scene: a close view of a judge's hand emptying a ballot urn onto a table, every ballot stone black, grim finality, a clerk recording the verdict
panels.composition: close, the black ballots of condemnation

bubbles.text: The ballots had been thrown; they were all black, and Justine was condemned.

bubbles.speaker: OFFICER
bubbles.text: Justine had already confessed her guilt

bubbles.speaker: OFFICER
bubbles.text: none of our judges like to condemn a criminal upon circumstantial evidence, be it ever so decisive

panels.scene: the golden-haired young woman with the braided bonnet at home by a dark window, stricken and disillusioned, hands clasped, grief and lost faith on her face

teen.narration: THE FALSE CONFESSION BREAKS ELIZABETH'S HEART.

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: How shall I ever again believe in human goodness?

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: Justine, whom I loved and esteemed as my sister, how could she put on those smiles of innocence only to betray?

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: Her mild eyes seemed incapable of any severity or guile, and yet she has committed a murder

panels.scene: a gloomy stone prison cell, the manacled servant woman in the white cap on a bed of straw throwing herself weeping at the feet of the golden-haired young woman with the braided bonnet, both grieving

teen.narration: IN THE CONDEMNED CELL, ELIZABETH AND VICTOR VISIT HER.

bubbles.text: her hands were manacled, and her head rested on her knees
she threw herself at the feet of Elizabeth, weeping bitterly

bubbles.speaker: ELIZABETH
bubbles.text: Why did you rob me of my last consolation? I relied on your innocence

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: I do not fear to die... God raises my weakness and gives me courage to endure the worst

panels.scene: a close view of the manacled servant woman in the white cap confessing through tears to the golden-haired young woman, anguish and shame, a dark priest's shadow looming on the cell wall behind her

teen.narration: JUSTINE CONFESSES THE TERRIBLE TRUTH — SHE LIED TO BE ABSOLVED.

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: I did confess, but I confessed a lie. I confessed, that I might obtain absolution

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: my confessor has besieged me; he threatened and menaced

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: he threatened excommunication and hell fire in my last moments if I continued obdurate

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: In an evil hour I subscribed to a lie; and now only am I truly miserable

panels.scene: the bespectacled dark-haired young man withdrawn into a shadowed corner of the cell, teeth gritted, fists clenched, silent unbearable guilt consuming him
panels.composition: close, the true murderer's silent hell

teen.narration: IN THE CORNER, THE TRUE MURDERER SUFFERS IN SILENCE.

bubbles.text: I, the true murderer, felt the never-dying worm alive in my bosom
I bore a hell within me which nothing could extinguish.
Anguish and despair had penetrated into the core of my heart

panels.scene: grey dawn over a bleak scaffold on a hill, birds scattering, the golden-haired young woman weeping below, a heavy stillness of grief and injustice
panels.composition: wide, the mournful morning of the execution

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: Farewell, sweet lady, dearest Elizabeth, my beloved and only friend

bubbles.speaker: JUSTINE
bubbles.text: Live, and be happy, and make others so.
And on the morrow Justine died.
She perished on the scaffold as a murderess!
